TK-LU01-LA04 | UNIT 1 LEARNING ACTIVITY

Protective layers

Select a coloured segment on the circle to see how each layer helps people respond safely. The strongest protection comes from the layers working together.

Why this matters:

Protection is layered, not individual

Personal awareness is important, but it is only one layer. Family readiness, sound operational controls and clear reporting support ensure that no one person must carry a safety threat alone.

Summary: build layers before you need them

Protection improves when personal habits, family conversations, organisational controls and trusted support are planned together. No layer needs to be perfect; the value comes from reinforcing one another.

Practical takeaway: Keep the trusted response contact available, agree a simple family check-in approach, and respect the controls that prevent any one person from acting alone under pressure.
